reason: Closure verdict holds. Independent re-tally of the scratchpad divtiming_out.json (56 exp60 clips, 99 GT divisions) reproduces every number: control 16/25/83 with exactly 83 FN rows listed (so the TP-fork proxy matches the official count), 31 FN with no fork within +-4 frames, 46 with the nearest fork >= 12 um away, 5 at 7-12 um (dt 0,+4,+4,+3,-4), 1 < 7 um (44b6_eb2880fc, dt +2, 2.07 um, fork labelled FP); FP forks: 15 with no GT divider within +-4 frames, 5 >= 12 um, 5 < 12 um with only eb2880fc under 7 um. ins35 (25/31/74) has the same shape. The official metric (division_metrics.py: max_distance 7.0 um; parent side = divider + predecessor, daughter side = child + grandchildren, fork = matched parent or its successor) already absorbs +-1 frame, so the forum's 'daughter one frame later' noise is priced in. The only extra reach is 1 fork (about 1/99 divisions); the 3 late forks at dt +3/+4 and 8-12 um would need a fork-timing shift, which is the closed forkmid family. Caveats that do not overturn it: the lab covers two train embryos only, so noise on hidden embryos could differ, but copying noise nobody has measured cannot be tested and is past the R8 hard line (27 Sep 12:00) anyway. 'No GT-free rule can pick that fork' is stated, not proven, but with a reach of 1 fork it does not matter. The division loss is missing forks, which matches round 8.
fix: Curator: set I-276 status to 'refuted (measured, round 9)' with the numbers above (FN reach 1/83, FP reach 1/25, metric window +-1 frame at 7 um). Word it as 'no measurable reach on the 2 train embryos', not as proof about hidden embryos. Keep at most a GT-annotation-audit study item on the post-deadline list, not a mechanism. No plan change; finals #37 + #38 stay as they are.
realistic_gain: 0. At most 1 of 99 GT divisions (1 FN plus 1 FP fork) on 56 lab clips. That is well under 0.001 on the division term, below anything the public LB can resolve, and nothing is submittable under R8.
